PullRequest.Title: automations: remember folders selected in workspace picker
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #340173.

## Change

Remove the automation workspace picker's false-returning `_shouldPersistSelection` override so accepted user selections use the same existing history path as the new-session picker. The production change is four deleted lines; no shared picker/service changes or new flags.

Initialization still passes `persist: false`, so opening an existing automation does not record a new pick. User picks update the recent folder's checked state just like new chat. This is remembered workspace history, not an unconditional replacement of an already-open session draft: existing picker restoration guards still apply.

Update regression coverage for recent ordering/checked state, accepted browsing, cancelled browsing, declined trust, and non-persisting initialization.

## Validation

Passed on Windows with Node 24.18.0 (reusing completed validation where inputs are unchanged):

- `npx.cmd --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -c "npm.cmd run build-fast -- --client-only"` — passed.
- `npx.cmd --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -c ".\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --grep AutomationsWorkspacePicker --reporter dot"` — 18 tests passed.
- `npx.cmd --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -c "npm.cmd run eslint -- src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\browser\automationDialog.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts"` — passed.
- `npx.cmd --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -c "npm.cmd run typecheck-client"` — passed.
- `git --no-pager diff --check` — passed before commit.

Manually verified in signed-in Code OSS: browse a previously absent local folder in the automation dialog, reopen its picker and see the folder in recents, cancel creation, and verify the folder appears in the new-session picker and a fresh automation dialog. No automation was scheduled or run. Remote-provider end-to-end behavior was not exercised.

## How to test

1. Open Automations in the Agents window and choose Create Automation.
2. Browse to a local folder absent from recent workspaces.
3. Reopen the workspace picker: the folder should appear in recents.
4. Close the dialog and verify the folder also appears on the new-session page and in a fresh automation dialog.
5. Cancel browsing or decline trust: history should not change.

The branch preserves the comparison build's base; fetched main is 76 commits ahead, with no changes to either file in this PR.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The complete synchronous event and session-creation path is present in repository code, the hidden NewChatView lifetime is explicitly preserved by the custom-view visibility implementation, and agent-host eager backend creation is explicit. Provider-specific backend cost varies, which affects magnitude but not the extra creation mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: An additional hidden draft session, including agent-host config/branch RPCs and an eager backend session creation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each accepted automation selection that changes the checked folder emits one shared recents event; while the covered NewChatView remains alive and has not been explicitly picked, every such event can replace its draft and eagerly create another backend. Rapidly trying several folders repeats this startup/churn once per accepted pick.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary backend startup, IPC/network work, and session replacement add resource contention and can delay the automation draft that the user actually selected.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: AutomationsWorkspacePicker overrode _shouldPersistSelection() to return false, so its accepted picks did not call addRecentWorkspace, did not broadcast onDidChangeRecentWorkspaces, and only the automation draft synchronizer created a session for the selected target.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Deleting the override makes the automation picker inherit true. WorkspacePicker._selectFolder now calls addRecentWorkspace; _persistRecentWorkspaces synchronously fires onDidChangeRecentWorkspaces, causing other live WorkspacePickers to run _restoreAutomaticSelection.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Removing AutomationsWorkspacePicker._shouldPersistSelection() at the deleted line changes its return value from false to the inherited true, newly activating the shared persistence/event path for automation selections.
Findings.Title: Do not start a hidden new-session backend when recording an automation pick
Findings.Impact: Open Automations from the Agents window and choose a different folder while the default new-session composer is covered by the custom view. SessionsPart only marks that composer invisible rather than disposing it, so its picker consumes the history event, fires onDidSelectWorkspace, and NewChatWidget.openNewSession creates a second, unseen draft. Agent-host providers then resolve config/load branches and call eagerCreate in addition to the intended automation session.
Findings.Evidence: The deleted override is the only guard preventing inherited persistence. The resulting call path is WorkspacePicker._selectFolder -> SessionsRecentWorkspacesService.addRecentWorkspace -> _persistRecentWorkspaces -> onDidChangeRecentWorkspaces -> hidden WorkspacePicker._restoreAutomaticSelection -> onDidSelectWorkspace -> NewChatWidget._onWorkspaceSelected -> SessionsService.openNewSession -> SessionsManagementService.createNewSession -> provider.createNewSession. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._createDraftSession explicitly invokes _startNewSessionBackend, which resolves config, loads branches, and calls newSession.eagerCreate(connection). Workbench._applyCustomViewGridVisibility merely calls SessionsPart.setContentVisible(false); NewChatView remains constructed and only updates its visibility observable, so this listener is live while the Automations custom view and dialog are open.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep storing the checked recent workspace, but prevent external history restoration from creating a draft in a suspended NewChatView—for example, apply the restored selection silently while inputVisible is false and defer _onWorkspaceSelected until that view becomes visible, or make the recents notification source-aware so inactive consumers do not run session-creation side effects.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the create/edit Automation dialog with an initial workspace or quick-chat target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog constructs MobileAutomationsWorkspacePicker and AutomationSessionDraftSynchronizer. Existing workspace initialization explicitly calls setSelectedWorkspace(..., persist: false), so no newly added history write or notification is on this path. Existing initial automation-draft setup remains on the dialog readiness path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Loads bounded VS Code recent-workspace metadata and reads up to 10 workspace files when the delayed service is first initialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 10 workspace-file reads on cold service initialization; none on a warm already-loaded service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same delayed recent-workspace service and bounded cold history load existed before the override was removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History loading is asynchronous and pre-existing; it is not newly placed on dialog initialization by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates the initial automation draft session/quick chat through the selected provider when a valid initial target exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one applied draft target after synchronizer coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The automation draft synchronizer created the same draft before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for configuration availability in the dialog; unchanged by the persistence override deletion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dialog and one initial target. Recent history is capped at 10 agent entries; VS Code workspace-history loading is independently capped at 10 workspace files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial picker restoration and automation draft synchronization use their existing sequencing. The PR adds no concurrency on initialization because persist remains false.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm profile storage/provider state avoids history or provider discovery costs; cold SessionsRecentWorkspacesService initialization may read bounded VS Code history/workspace files, but that behavior and its cache lifecycle are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the explicit persist:false call and unchanged synchronizer path are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific draft setup cost varies, but no changed initialization mechanism is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No initialization regression; the new inherited persistence path is not reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accept a different recent or browsed workspace in the Automation picker while the Automations custom view covers the default new-session view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After browse/connect/trust succeeds, WorkspacePicker._selectFolder now persists before firing the automation picker's own selection event. The shared recents notification synchronously reaches the still-live hidden NewChatView picker, which restores the newly checked folder and starts a standard new-session draft; the automation listener then also starts the intended automation draft.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads and serializes the bounded recent list, clears the no-workspace key, conditionally updates excluded-folder storage, and stores the checked recent entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded recent-list write plus key updates per accepted pick; at most 10 serialized entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automation picks were blocked by _shouldPersistSelection() and performed no profile-storage update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the automation selection event, but is small and bounded by 10 entries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The covered, still-live new-session composer creates/replaces a standard draft for the externally checked workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra hidden draft per accepted changed automation pick while the hidden picker remains eligible for automatic restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without an automation-originated recents event, the covered new-session picker did not restore this folder or create this draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts from the synchronous history notification and can contend with the intended automation draft despite being invisible to the user.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolves session config, loads branches, and calls newSession.eagerCreate(connection) for the extra hidden draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra config/branch/backend startup for each hidden draft; it may overlap the intended automation draft startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the intended automation session was created for an automation picker selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Consumes provider/backend resources and may delay the session the dialog actually needs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates the intended automation session for the selected folder and captures/replaces configuration when retargeting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One applied automation target after local coalescing, with capture when replacing an existing target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same intended automation draft was created before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required dialog work and potentially overlaps the newly triggered hidden draft.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Shows the local folder dialog and, when required, performs the existing workspace-trust flow before applying the selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browse dialog and at most one trust request per browse attempt; absent when choosing an existing recent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Browsing and trust validation already preceded automation workspace selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before any selection is applied; unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One shared notification per accepted selection. The stored list is capped at 10, but each accepted different folder can replace and restart the hidden draft; repeated trial selections therefore repeat the extra backend startup once per accepted pick.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The recents event dispatch is synchronous. NewChatWidget starts its async session creation from that event, then the automation draft synchronizer starts its own provider session; their config, branch, and eager backend work can overlap. Each component has local cancellation/coalescing, but there is no shared limiter preventing the two distinct drafts, and a backend may already have started before a later pick replaces it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm profile storage only reduces persistence latency; it does not suppress the event. A warm agent connection makes eagerCreate immediately reachable, while a cold/auth-pending connection defers it until connection/auth settles. No cache or deduplication coalesces the hidden standard draft with the automation draft because they use separate management slots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: custom-view visibility suspends rather than disposes NewChatView, the shared event-to-openNewSession call chain is direct, and agent-host eager backend creation is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact backend startup time and whether the provider is local or remote vary, but agent-host eager creation and branch/config work are explicit. The common trigger requires the covered default NewChatView to be alive and not explicitly user-picked, which is the default custom-view transition but not every possible layout state.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out: one automation pick newly starts a second hidden session/backend.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel folder browsing or decline workspace trust in the Automation picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browse action or trust decision completes, _dispatchPickerItem returns false before _selectFolder, and neither persistence nor either selection event runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Shows the local filesystem folder picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical browse operation before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user must finish or cancel it before dispatch returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Requests workspace trust for a selected folder when the resolved workspace requires it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per returned folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical trust gate before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must be accepted before selection; decline prevents all persistence and session creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user browse attempt; no recent-list or session cardinality after cancellation/decline.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new draft synchronization is scheduled from the rejected selection. Existing browse/trust work is serialized with picker dispatch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage and provider caches are irrelevant because the newly enabled persistence path is not reached. Previously trusted folders bypass the trust prompt, but an accepted folder then follows the reported scenario instead.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: generation, folder, and trust checks all precede _selectFolder in the dispatch path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality; cancellation and decline are directly guarded before _selectFolder.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on cancelled or declined attempts; tests correctly establish that the new persistence path is not reached.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced initialization, accepted selection, browse cancellation, trust decline, shared storage events, hidden-view lifecycle, and provider draft creation. One diff-introduced boundary-fanout finding was submitted: recording an automation pick can eagerly create an additional hidden standard session/backend.
